note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see edge/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: LUXE's fiscal Q4 is the quarter ended 30 June 2026 — exactly the window in which Richemont reported group sales +20% at constant rates with online retail +18% (quarter ended 30 June 2026), Kering posted +2% comparable for its first positive quarter in three years, and LVMH's Fashion & Leather Goods returned to +1% organic for the first time in seven quarters, with double-digit growth from American shoppers; LUXE's own Q3 (to March) was flat ex-FX and management blamed 'geopolitical headwinds in March', so the demand comparison inverts inside the reported quarter.

3.95m LUXE shares are sold short against an average daily volume of roughly 109k-125k shares, i.e. 31.6 to 34.3 days to cover, on a reported free float of 17.19m shares out of 137.26m outstanding (Richemont alone holds 49,741,342 consideration shares) — an extreme days-to-cover for a $980m name going into a binary bmo print.

The FY26 headline is arithmetically pre-determined: H1 FY26 GMV was EUR1,230.6m and Q3 segment GMV sums to EUR653.7m (Mytheresa 279.6 + NAP&MRP 243.4 + YOOX 130.7), so against the confirmed FY26 guide of EUR2.5-2.7bn GMV, Q4 needs only about EUR616m versus a EUR654m Q3 run-rate to clear the bottom; on margin, 9M adjusted EBITDA is about EUR0.9m on EUR1,838.8m of net sales (+0.05%) against a -1% to +1% FY guide, and the CFO said on 19 May that Q4 adjusted EBITDA would be 'similar to Q3 levels', then on 14 September told the Goldman Sachs Global Consumer and Retail Conference that Mytheresa had already delivered roughly a 6% adjusted EBITDA margin for FY26.

Both luxury sites are losing traffic rank through the quarter the FY27 guide will be written off: mytheresa.com's global rank fell from #6,112 to #6,699 over the three months to August 2026 with visits -6.5% month-on-month, and net-a-porter.com sat at global rank #7,675 in August 2026 with visits -8.11% month-on-month.

findings.finding: EPM's net commodity-derivative position was a $6.26m liability at 3/31/2026 when WTI settled at $102.86; WTI closed the June quarter at $70.56, so the hedge book (oil swaps at $60.24 and $65.12, collar ceilings $64.11/$69.37/$70.36, plus gas swaps at $3.62/$3.57) must mark back toward zero and throw off roughly a $4-5m non-cash unrealized GAAP gain in fiscal Q4 — the mirror image of the $7.6m unrealized loss that produced the $(0.26) GAAP print and the -12.11% reaction on 2026-05-12 — against a normalised consensus of $0.01 that excludes marks.

The 2026-08-19 prospectus supplement discloses that at 6/30/2026 EPM had cash of $6.1m and credit-facility borrowings of $56.5m — debt unchanged from 3/31/2026 while cash rose from $2.6m — meaning the June quarter generated roughly $7.8m after paying the $4.26m quarterly dividend, comfortably the best coverage quarter of FY2026 for a stock yielding 12.7% whose entire equity story is the 52-quarter dividend streak.

findings.finding: The bearish Chinese-travel datapoint circulating since 2026-08-31 — Flight Master's projection that Chinese carriers' July+August traffic would fall 3.6% y/y to 142m, 'the first contraction in the peak season since 2022' — is contradicted by CAAC's actual July 2026 print published ten days earlier: 74.63m passenger trips, +3.9% y/y, domestic +4.1%, international +2.3%; and forward bookings measured by 2026-09-08 for the unusual 13-day 25 Sep-7 Oct holiday window show 6.06m domestic air tickets (+~14% y/y) and 2.07m international/cross-border (+~7% y/y), with multi-destination trips +25% y/y.

China industry hotel RevPAR fell ~6% y/y in July 2026 (occupancy -3pp, ADR -1%) and Hilton cut its full-year China RevPAR outlook from roughly flat to a low-single-digit decline — a rate/ADR deflation that lands on Trip.com's highest-take-rate line, accommodation reservation (RMB6.5bn and +17% y/y in Q1 2026), and that post-dates the 2026-06-24 guidance, so tonight's Q3 outlook is the first management commentary to incorporate it.

findings.finding: Charlie's Holdings' shareholder letter of 2026-09-09 - seven days before Ispire's print - says the age-gated launch is still only a 'pilot test ... this fall' and that shipping waits on Ispire's side ('As soon as IKE's software developers complete their final tests of the consumer app, we will begin shipping'), against Ispire CEO Michael Wang telling the 2026-02-06 call that Charlie's would launch 'in the next two to three months' at 'between 2 million chips a month and 3 million chips a month' and 'we should start seeing results in the next quarter' - i.e. exactly the Apr-Jun fiscal Q4 being reported on 09-16.

The 'significant development deal around our age-gating technology with a leading global nicotine company in the coming weeks' that Michael Wang promised on the 2026-02-06 call has not been announced in the seven months since: Ispire's own press-release index runs 2026-02-04 to 2026-08-17 with nothing of the kind (the only deal in the gap is the Jincheng Pharma nicotine-pouch JV, a Chinese pharma manufacturing tie-up, not an age-gating licence), and the 2026-05-07 Q3 call did not mention the deal, Charlie's, iQTEC or chip volumes at all.

Michael Wang - the executive who made both the chip-volume and the 'coming weeks' claims and who ran the growth narrative on the calls - was removed as Co-CEO effective 2026-07-16 and pushed down to running the Aspire North America subsidiary, disclosed in an 8-K carrying Item 5.02 only, with no Item 7.01 and no press release; three weeks later the Przybyla promotion to President got Items 5.02 AND 7.01 plus a PR Newswire release. Tuanfang Liu, the China-based founder-chairman, is now sole CEO.

Fiscal Q4 is the audited quarter and the receivable book is already 43% reserved: at 2026-03-31 gross accounts receivable were $50,151,620 against an allowance for credit losses of $21,500,062, with $5,564,497 of bad-debt expense in fiscal Q3 alone and $11,537,950 over nine months, while working capital had fallen to roughly $0.8m (current assets $55.7m vs current liabilities $54.9m) from $9.3m two quarters earlier and cash fell from $24.35m to $18.03m.
